A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same MoDGS research work and complete 27-page documents, including Appendix A.1–A.20. Text, equations, tables and figures support a reliable comparison after accounting for page reflow.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A report original novel-view synthesis experiments, quantitative comparisons, ablations and robustness analyses.

after.justification: The same original experimental results remain in Section 4 and Appendix A, including PSNR, SSIM and LPIPS measurements and qualitative reconstructions.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 retain the same canonical Gaussians, invertible deformation network, 3D-aware initialization, ordinal depth loss and training procedure.

E1.justification: Both retain the same DyNeRF, Nvidia, MCV and DAVIS evaluations, alongside the same appendix scenarios involving complex motion, rapid motion and camera-pose diagnostics.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: Table 1 retains HexPlane, SC-GS and Deformable-GS; Figure 6 also includes RoDynRF; Appendix A.6 retains Shape-of-Motion. The other appendix comparisons also match.

E3.justification: Training/test camera choices, scale alignment and PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS evaluation in Section 4.1 are unchanged. Training budgets, preprocessing and appendix experimental settings also match.

E4.justification: The same initialization and loss ablations, alpha sensitivity, depth-noise tests, depth-estimator comparisons and motion case studies remain in Section 4.3 and Appendix A.

E5.justification: Both report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. No experimental uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Tables 1–13 and the qualitative figures retain the same results. For example, Table 1 reports MoDGS PSNR of 22.64 on DyNeRF and 19.27 on Nvidia in both versions.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6, the depth-order definition and the Pearson/scale-shift loss equivalence derivation in Appendix A.5 are unchanged. Their repositioning introduces no mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and performance claims for casual-monocular view synthesis using 3D-aware initialization and ordinal depth supervision.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and limitations remain unchanged, including unseen regions, training cost, depth and pose errors, complex motion, specular surfaces and low-light conditions.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1–A.2 retains the same implementation and preprocessing details, including PyTorch, Adam, the 20k-plus-20k training schedule, loss settings and RTX A6000 resource information. The project-page link is unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works and positioning relative to prior and concurrent methods are unchanged. Bibliographic entries merely reflow across pages.

P1.justification: The marginal arXiv version/date text changes from v3, 17 May 2025, to v4, 31 August 2026. Prose, terminology, section order and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: All 17 figures and 13 tables are retained, with limited spacing and page-flow changes. The explanation after Equation 3 moves onto page 6, eliminating its overlap with the Section 3.4 heading on page 7; the conclusion now fits on page 10.

improvement.justification: v4 provides a small readability improvement by removing the visible overlap near Section 3.4 and keeping the conclusion together. Scientific content, experimental evidence and reproducibility information are unchanged, so the quality gain is limited to presentation.
